scores.claim_text: KC-46A USAF prime contract awarded 2011; authorized LRIP lots ~$32B as of Dec 31, 2025; options for 179 aircraft.
scores.M_value: Mode A: top DoD award 'KC-X MODERNIZATION PROGRAM' FA862511C6600 $31.96B obligated to THE BOEING COMPANY (matches ~$32B disclosed). Boeing has 98,895 DoD awards totaling $209.5B. Mode B: KC-46A Tanker Squadrons PE 0401221F status FUNDED_GROWING; FY24 $78.7M, FY25 $77.8M, FY26 $145.4M procurement uptrend.
scores.interpretation: Registry confirms KC-46A contract dollar magnitude precisely matches 10-K disclosure ($31.96B Award vs $32B authorized LRIP). J-Book shows program funded and growing through FY26. PASS on both modes.

scores.claim_text: MQ-25 Stingray EMD contract from U.S. Navy Q3 2018, fixed-price $890M, 7 aircraft + test articles.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts Boeing (Mode A) + pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding MQ-25 (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: Boeing has dozens of Navy awards in DoD obligation data; specific MQ-25 prime relationship is well-established (Navy prime). Mode B: pentagon_jbook 'MQ-25' returned NOT_FOUND in the J-Book corpus — program not yet hand-extracted; cannot verify forward PB funding trajectory.
scores.interpretation: Mode A confirms Boeing-Navy contracting at the corporate level (consistent with MQ-25 award). Mode B is a coverage gap (J-Book corpus does not include MQ-25 program line) — cannot verify whether MQ-25 procurement is forward-funded in the most-recent PB. Heuristic 5 partially applies but for a fixed-price loss program like MQ-25 (Boeing has recorded reach-forward losses on MQ-25), forward-funding visibility would have been useful. Net: MODERATE underdelivery on coverage.

scores.claim_text: T-7A Red Hawk USAF program; production probable for 342 aircraft; $860M EMD; first deliveries in 2025; USAF updated acquisition approach Jan 2025.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts Boeing (Mode A) + pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding T-7A (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: Boeing has $209.5B in DoD awards including a wide variety of USAF program codes (KC-46, F-15, B-52, etc.) consistent with USAF prime status. Mode B: pentagon_jbook 'T-7A' returned NOT_FOUND in the J-Book corpus — program-line PE not yet extracted.
scores.interpretation: Mode A general DoD contracting confirmed at corporate level; Mode B is unable to verify whether the 342-aircraft production assumption is forward-supported by recent PB lines (this is the key delta — the 342 is Boeing's expectation, not contracted). Heuristic 10 applies (IDIQ-style production assumption vs obligated). MODERATE underdelivery.

scores.claim_text: VC-25B Presidential Aircraft (Air Force One) $4B program; 2 modified 747-8 aircraft.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts Boeing (Mode A) + pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding VC-25 (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: Boeing top-tier DoD prime with USAF contracts evident in $209.5B obligation total. Mode B: VC-25B PE 0401319F status FUNDED_GROWING; FY24 $94.75M, FY25 $433.94M, FY26 $602.32M — strong upward funding trajectory in newest PB.
scores.interpretation: Both modes pass cleanly. PB funding is accelerating (6x in two years) consistent with Boeing's reach-forward loss disclosures indicating ongoing work. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Spirit AeroSystems acquisition closed Dec 8, 2025 (~$4.7B stock); Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture closed Oct 31, 2025 ($10.55B cash).
scores.M_value: Mode A: Boeing 8-K filings extensively cover M&A activity; the Spirit acquisition and DAS divestiture are widely confirmed in SEC filings. Mode B: acq_coherence LLM returned coherence_score 0.0 because the test harness did not surface the rationale to the model (insufficient input detail), with reasoning explicitly saying 'cannot assess'. This is a tooling artifact, not a real low-coherence finding — re-acquiring a sole-source 737 fuselage supplier you previously spun off is textbook supply-chain vertical integration in response to the 737-9 door plug crisis.
scores.interpretation: Strategic coherence is high (sole-source supplier reintegration after quality crisis at a once-spun-off subsidiary). Mode B LLM scoring is uninformative due to insufficient context surfaced; the structural logic is sound. PASS on Mode A; Mode B is a tooling no-op rather than a negative signal.

scores.claim_text: Q4 2024 equity raise: $18.2B common stock + $5.7B Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (~$23.9B total, net of issuance costs).
scores.M_value: Mode A: 4 x 424B5 filings on Oct 28-29, 2024 (accessions 0001193125-24-244582/244584/246629/246634) confirming concurrent common + MCPS offerings — matches 10-K disclosure exactly. Mode B: 90 Form 4 filings, 35 total insider sales totaling $18.86M, 0 proximate to budget/raise events, signal=NO_PROXIMATE_SALES. No CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY flag.
scores.interpretation: Equity raise documented in SEC filings on exact dates. Insider sales registry shows NO suspicious clustering around the raise or PB releases — the absence-of-bad-signal is itself confirmatory. PASS on both modes.

scores.claim_text: 111 million sq ft facility footprint (86% US); workforce ~182,000; major BDS sites at St. Louis MO, Seattle WA, Mesa AZ, Huntsville AL, Philadelphia PA, etc.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities WA (Mode A) + osha_establishments.query_establishments Boeing (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: EPA FRS returns 93 BOEING-named facilities in Washington alone (Seattle/Tukwila/Everett etc.) — consistent with disclosed Seattle BCA footprint. Mode B: OSHA returns 142 Boeing-related establishments across WA, MO, AK and other states; includes Boeing manufacturing and contractor sites consistent with disclosed major locations.
scores.interpretation: Disclosed physical footprint corroborated at multiple registries. Boeing has one of the most heavily-documented industrial footprints in U.S. federal databases. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Boeing owns a large patent portfolio relating to its products and manufacture, with USG licenses to government-contract-derived patents.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee 'The Boeing Company' (Mode A) + uspto_odp.query_assignee 'Spirit AeroSystems' (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: Boeing has 10,536 granted patents and 16,569 total applications under the assignee 'The Boeing Company' — among the largest corporate portfolios in the U.S. Mode B: Newly-acquired Spirit AeroSystems brings an additional 118 granted patents (250 applications) into the rollup. Recent Boeing filings include emergency exit door, wiring harness anomaly detection, and composite-forming technologies — all aerospace core.
scores.interpretation: Patent registry confirms 'large portfolio' claim by 3 orders of magnitude (per heuristic 8, n_granted >= 5 with category hit is PASS; here 10,536). Combined entity ~10,654 granted patents. PASS.

scores.claim_text: NASA contracted Boeing to build CST-100 Starliner; Crewed Flight Test launched June 5, 2024 and docked with ISS.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts Boeing (Mode A) + nasa_ntrs.query_ntrs 'Starliner CST-100 Boeing' (Mode B)
scores.M_value: Mode A: USAspending recipient_contracts shows NAS1510000 to THE BOEING COMPANY from NASA totaling $22.43B for 'INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION' — confirms NASA prime relationship and ISS programmatic context that Starliner serves. Mode B: NTRS query returned 9 total / 0 filtered with NASA_NO_FOOTPRINT — Commercial Crew is operational rather than research output, so NTRS coverage gap is expected (heuristic 5/calibration).
scores.interpretation: Mode A massively corroborates NASA-Boeing prime relationship with $22.4B obligated for ISS. Mode B coverage gap on operational programs is normal — NTRS is a research-publication corpus and Commercial Crew is operational delivery. PASS.

scores.M_value: Mode A: 11 UEIs resolve under Boeing variants with top UEI showing $23.24B FY snapshot — peer-prime scale; 99,311 recipient contracts totaling $235.7B all-time. Mode B: 20 hits for 'Boeing' in Northrop Grumman SEC filings spanning 8-K, DEF 14A from 2018-2026 — Northrop discloses Boeing as a competitor/counterparty in its proxy/risk filings consistently.
